newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Rouble eases on fund inflow from T-bill market.
newsitem.headline: Rouble eases on fund inflow from T-bill market.

text.p: The rouble eased in calm trading on Wednesday as funds flowed in from the government bond market, dealers said.

"The dollar is near the upper limit of the central bank's rates. There are plenty of roubles on the market as today's (T-bill) auctions seem less attractive. Banks could be also selling T-bills," one dealer said.
The central bank will auction on Wednesday eight trillion roubles of new six-month paper and an additional tranche of three trillion roubles of six-month bills.
Konversbank dealer Stanislav Belov said overnight rouble credit rates were higher in early trade because banks had expected higher rouble demand, as happened last Wednesday.
"But now roubles are cheap, dollars are expensive and the market is too calm," he said.

Roubles for today settlement were quoted at 5,483-84 per dollar compared with an early 5,481-83 and 5,474-76 late on Tuesday. Tomorrow roubles eased to 5,482-84 per dollar from Tuesday's late 5,478-80.
The central bank said it had set 5,473/5,483 as its bid and offer rates against the dollar on Wednesday.
Overnight rouble credits yielded 5-10 percent. Yields were 10-20 percent in early trading and late on Tuesday.
